entities.summary: Gnaeus Fulvius Centumalus was a Roman consul in 229 BC, who played a key role in the First Illyrian War against Queen Teuta. Born in an unknown location, he served alongside Lucius Postumius Albinus and led part of the Roman forces in their campaign against the Illyrian kingdom. The war had significant consequences for the Roman Republic, including the acquisition of new territories and resources. Despite being a notable figure in Roman history, Gnaeus Fulvius Centumalus has largely been overshadowed by his contemporaries. He is best remembered for his military achievements, particularly his victory over Queen Teuta's forces in the Battle of the Aegimurus. This battle marked a turning point in the war and secured a vital Roman victory. Centumalus' legacy is also notable for its impact on Roman diplomacy and foreign policy, as it demonstrated the effectiveness of Roman military strategy and tactics. The Roman victory in the First Illyrian War paved the way for future Roman expansion and cemented Rome's position as a dominant power in the Mediterranean region.
